## Post

Your project plan shouldn't need a project manager to maintain it.

Most small projects end up in a spreadsheet: a kitchen renovation, a website launch, a trade show. It works
until one task slips, a bank holiday falls in the middle, and every date after it has to be moved by hand.

So I built a Gantt planner you type one line per task:
→ "Install cabinets 12/12 3d after 7" creates the task, its bar and its dependency.
→ Weekends and public holidays are skipped automatically: England and Wales, the US or France, recalculated
every year.
→ The critical path shows in red: the tasks where one day of delay moves your finish date.

It also tracks progress against what you should have done by today, keeps a baseline to compare with, and
prints the whole plan on one A4 or A3 page.

It opens in the browser, syncs across your computer and phone, and it's a one-time purchase, no
subscription.

Try the demo (no sign-up, nothing sent): qm-engineering.fr/en/templates
